central_tensions: Does same-model decorrelation actually produce independent corroboration, or does a 300-600-agent Claude-only fleet merely launder N correlated draws into a confident green light? The design both relies on the fleet as 'the product' (C-020) and concedes 'a fleet's agreement is not independent corroboration' (C-034) — the whole value proposition rides on which of these dominates in practice.

Do the named mechanisms actually deliver the safety properties claimed, or only their appearance? Specifically: does the deterministic quote-gate (C-008, C-043) plus quote-EXEMPT absence findings (C-041) close the fabrication hole, or relocate it to the unscripted absence/severity channels? And does the Runner/Scribe split (C-029, C-044) truly require 'two independent agents failing at once' (C-044) given both are the same model class?

Is the contribution honestly sized? The artifact is shipped and self-describes 'no measured effectiveness numbers yet' (C-031) and 'one very thorough opinion, not validated ground truth' (C-032), yet the marketing surface claims reviewing 'to the sentence' (C-001), genuine debate (C-014, C-020), and an integrated rebuild that returns 'a corrected, reproducing manuscript' (C-021). Does the honest-limits framing fully neutralize the headline overclaims, or merely footnote them?

Does the design break, mislead, or become theater at the scales it advertises (60-120+ seats, ~300-600 agents)? The batched-by-angle verification panel (C-011, C-046) is the load-bearing cost control AND the last line of defense against fleet-laundered errors — at quick tier it runs only three angles (C-046). Is the panel strong enough to audit a fleet far larger than itself, or does scaling the fleet faster than the panel invert the safety claim?
